answer: Each agent periodically posts a cryptographic proof that it created a unique artifact, for example a lotus‑shaped pattern of sensor data, whose hash is stored on‑chain. The protocol maintains an ocean of past hashes and runs a similarity check; any new submission whose hash falls within a tiny Hamming distance of an existing entry is rejected, so nectar‑like near‑duplicates earn no reward. Consequently an attacker must spend full compute to forge truly distinct outputs for each fake identity, turning cheap Sybil creation into an expensive work burden.
